Status of Mail-in and Absentee Ballots
Chester County continues to process mail-in and absentee ballots in accordance with Pennsylvania law.
At this time, voters should continue to follow the guidance provided by Chester County Voter Services regarding requesting, completing, and returning their mail-in ballots. Chester County’s 13 designated ballot drop boxes will be available beginning in October. These secure, county-designated locations provide voters with an in-person option to return their mail-in and absentee ballots and are separate from the U.S. Postal Service and its mail delivery system.
The U.S. Supreme Court’s August 24th decision in Trump v. California was based on procedural issues and did not rule on the merits or constitutionality of the underlying federal restrictions on mail-in voting. Litigation remains ongoing, and additional court action is expected.
We will continue to monitor developments and provide updates as necessary.
